Binding match states

Understand disk evidence, inventory matches and the actions a finding needs.

Review bindings
More actions

A binding is one certificate/key pair that a virtual host is configured to use on a server. Discovery compares what is on disk with the certificate inventory and records a match state. The dashboard only reports these states: it does not fix them, because correcting a server's files is your decision.

These are stored observations, not desired-deployment or live TLS verdicts. A matched certificate need not be the certificate you intend to deploy. Stale means the latest discovery did not succeed, not that this certificate changed.

matched
The certificate file on disk is a certificate in the inventory and the key at the configured path belongs to it.
unknown
The certificate file on disk is not in the inventory. Import it to track it.
 Drift: key_mismatch

The private key at the configured path does not belong to the certificate at the configured path. The web server would fail to start or reload with this pair.

The dashboard does not fix this. Check the virtual host's ssl_certificate_key (nginx) or SSLCertificateKeyFile (Apache) setting and the files on the server, put the right key in place, then run discovery again.

While a binding is in this state, the dashboard blocks deploys of that virtual host so a new certificate is never written next to a key that does not match.

 File failure: missing_file

The certificate file named in the configuration is missing or could not be read when the server was last discovered.

The dashboard does not fix this. Check the path in the configuration and the file's owner and mode on the server, restore the file or correct the path, then run discovery again.

Rotation is a command-line operation; this page never edits the keyring or rotates keys. Current state:

Active version 1; loaded versions: 1

Run these on the dashboard host as root (full procedure: docs/operations.md, section 6). Take a database backup first.

Generate the next version into a new file in a temporary 0700 directory owned by the container user, merging the current keyring (live limit: two versions). The current master_key is mounted read-only at /secrets and the new file is written to /out; both paths exist only inside this one docker run:
set -eu
tmp="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cert-dashboard-keyring.XXXXXXXX)"
install -d -m 0700 -o 10001 -g 10001 "$tmp"
docker run --rm -v /etc/cert-dashboard/secrets:/secrets:ro -v "$tmp":/out cert-dashboard:local \
  python -m app.cli generate-master-key --version 2 --merge /secrets/master_key --output /out/master_key.v2.new
sha256sum "$tmp/master_key.v2.new"
The command prints only sha256=<digest> path=<file>; the digest must equal the sha256sum output.
Keep a copy of the old file in the backup location, install the verified file as the master_key secret and restart so new writes use it:
install -m 0400 -o 10001 -g 10001 "$tmp/master_key.v2.new" /etc/cert-dashboard/secrets/master_key
shred -u -- "$tmp/master_key.v2.new" && rmdir -- "$tmp"
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web worker
Re-encrypt every key and TOTP seed (batched, idempotent, resumable):
docker compose run --rm web python -m app.cli rotate-master-key
Verify a keyed certificate (metadata only is printed):
docker compose run --rm web python -m app.cli verify-key --certificate-id ID

Secret files are read once at startup: replace the file, rerun scripts/install-secrets.sh and restart the service.

Run these on the dashboard host as root (full procedure: docs/operations.md, section 6). Take a database backup first.

Generate the next version into a new file in a temporary 0700 directory owned by the container user, merging the current keyring (live limit: two versions). The current master_key is mounted read-only at /secrets and the new file is written to /out; both paths exist only inside this one docker run:
set -eu
tmp="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cert-dashboard-keyring.XXXXXXXX)"
install -d -m 0700 -o 10001 -g 10001 "$tmp"
docker run --rm -v /etc/cert-dashboard/secrets:/secrets:ro -v "$tmp":/out cert-dashboard:local \
  python -m app.cli generate-master-key --version 2 --merge /secrets/master_key --output /out/master_key.v2.new
sha256sum "$tmp/master_key.v2.new"
The command prints only sha256=<digest> path=<file>; the digest must equal the sha256sum output.
Keep a copy of the old file in the backup location, install the verified file as the master_key secret and restart so new writes use it:
install -m 0400 -o 10001 -g 10001 "$tmp/master_key.v2.new" /etc/cert-dashboard/secrets/master_key
shred -u -- "$tmp/master_key.v2.new" && rmdir -- "$tmp"
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web worker
Re-encrypt every key and TOTP seed (batched, idempotent, resumable):
docker compose run --rm web python -m app.cli rotate-master-key
Verify a keyed certificate (metadata only is printed):
docker compose run --rm web python -m app.cli verify-key --certificate-id ID

Master key rotation

Rotation is a command-line operation; this page never edits the keyring or rotates keys. Current state:

Active version 1; loaded versions: 1
Rows not yet on the active version: 0

Run these on the dashboard host as root (full procedure: docs/operations.md, section 6). Take a database backup first.

Generate the next version into a new file in a temporary 0700 directory owned by the container user, merging the current keyring (live limit: two versions). The current master_key is mounted read-only at /secrets and the new file is written to /out; both paths exist only inside this one docker run:
set -eu
tmp="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cert-dashboard-keyring.XXXXXXXX)"
install -d -m 0700 -o 10001 -g 10001 "$tmp"
docker run --rm -v /etc/cert-dashboard/secrets:/secrets:ro -v "$tmp":/out cert-dashboard:local \
  python -m app.cli generate-master-key --version 2 --merge /secrets/master_key --output /out/master_key.v2.new
sha256sum "$tmp/master_key.v2.new"
The command prints only sha256=<digest> path=<file>; the digest must equal the sha256sum output.
Keep a copy of the old file in the backup location, install the verified file as the master_key secret and restart so new writes use it:
install -m 0400 -o 10001 -g 10001 "$tmp/master_key.v2.new" /etc/cert-dashboard/secrets/master_key
shred -u -- "$tmp/master_key.v2.new" && rmdir -- "$tmp"
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web worker
Re-encrypt every key and TOTP seed (batched, idempotent, resumable):
docker compose run --rm web python -m app.cli rotate-master-key
Verify a keyed certificate (metadata only is printed):
docker compose run --rm web python -m app.cli verify-key --certificate-id ID

Secret files are read once at startup: replace the file, rerun scripts/install-secrets.sh and restart the service.
